newsitem.title: UK: Markka ERM rate should cause no problems-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Markka ERM rate should cause no problems-analysts.

text.p: Finland's decision to join the European exchange rate mechanism is a sustainable policy and the central rate of 3.04 markka to the mark is a sensible level, London based financial analysts said.
"Everyone was assuming the markka was going to join soon with a central rate of around 3.03 (per mark) so this is not a huge surprise," said Stephen King, international economist at HSBC Markets.
Finland will join on Monday, October 14 and the markka central rate was set at FIM 5.80661 per ECU.

London analysts said Finland is in good shape to join with the economy back on track after the problems caused by the collapse of the Soviet Union, a major export market for Finland, and the economic backdrop looks quite good at the moment.
One cloud on the horizon could be the fact that with both Sweden and Norway not in the system, problems could occur for the markka if, for example, Sweden were to allow its currency to weaken.
Sweden's ruling Social Democratic Party has said it will decide at a congress next year if it is to link the crown to the exchange rate mechanism or seek to join EMU (economic and monetary union).
Analysts said the markka will probably rally quite strongly first thing on Monday simply because some of the downside risk has been removed now the currency is in the system.
The ERM was revamped in 1993 after a speculative attack by the foreign exchange market and fluctuation bands were widened to a yawning 15 percent either side of the central rate.
This gives the markka plenty of elbow room and it is extremely unlikely to get close to either the upper or lower limit, analysts said.
"This is a step in the right direction and I'm sure the Germans and the French are going to be happy about this decision," HSBC's" King said.

The move is bound to lead to intense speculation that Italy will also join the ERM soon so the lira will likely rally strongly on Monday as well. Italy is expected to take the ERM plunge by the end of the year.
